title: 'Free UI Cards': one profile structure in two skins (header image and full-bleed gradient)
attribution_visible_in_image: Visible text: 'Free UI Cards', Figma logo, 'figma.com/@Spline', 'spline.one'. Likely the publisher/creator; not confirmed.
contains_third_party_content: Photos of people; an Adobe logo inside the company chip.

observed.layout: Two 'Creative Director' cards on a dark-to-grey gradient page. Left: dark card with a warm blurred-gradient header, overlapping avatar with a green online dot, an 'Adobe Co.' chip, name/role, a bookmark-add button, an outlined stats strip (star 5.0 Rating; flag $160 hours; clock 24 Month) and a full-width white 'Get In Touch' button. Right: same structure over a full-bleed red/blue gradient with a dark silhouette and translucent glass chips and stats panel.
observed.hierarchy: Name, then the white CTA; stats are tertiary.
observed.typography: Neutral grotesk; bold names, small grey roles. Unconfirmed.
observed.iconography: Colored mini icons (yellow star, blue flag, purple clock).
observed.materials: Left: solid dark card. Right: gradient photo with glass overlays.

interpretation.aesthetic: Free UI-kit presentation; two skins on a shared structure.
implementation_notes: Same component, two backgrounds: header-image vs full-bleed with backdrop-filter glass overlays.
White CTA stays constant across skins for recognition.
interpretation.caveat: Stats read '$160 / hours' and '24 / Month'. The intended meaning is probably rate per hour and 24 months of experience, but the labels as written are ambiguous.

concept_work.essence: One information architecture, two moods, with the CTA constant.
what_makes_it_work: Structure survives a very different background.
Avatar overlap links the header and body.
gaps_to_make_it_work: On the red card, small light labels over saturated red measure about 2.5:1.
Bookmark button purpose is unclear without a label.

pattern.name: One card structure, two skins (header image vs full-bleed)
use_when: Cards with a single contact/hire CTA
avoid_when: Photos or backgrounds are unpredictable and no scrim is possible
must_preserve: Scrim behind text on gradients or photos
adaptation_examples: Freelancer card: '$160 / hour' and '24 mo experience'.
Speaker card: stats become talks given and rating.
failure_modes: Light text on saturated color near 2.5:1
Duplicate information across chip and stats

lessons: Keep the CTA constant when changing the skin.
Make value and label read as one phrase ('$160 / hour').

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: Dark neutral page; saturated red/blue only inside the right card; white CTA is the highest-contrast element in both.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: A hire/contact card with a clear CTA and credentials.
Strong contrast between the two skins and consistent structure.
Card conventions are followed, but stat labels are ambiguous or inverted, which hurts semantic correctness.
One CTA is clear; bookmark and chip behavior are unspecified; no hover/disabled states.
Both cards share the same spacing, radii and component layout.
Two skins on one structure is useful but the card patterns themselves are familiar.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 16.43:1; secondary text min 2.41:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
